findings.explanation: Lean proves by reflexivity that `fresh UNIV` equals the Hilbert-selected function satisfying the freshness specification applied to `UNIV`. HOL4 saves only the property that `fresh s` lies outside each finite `s`. The set of all strings is infinite, so changing a witness at `UNIV` to any string preserves the saved property. The Lean equation fixes a value that this property leaves open.
findings.repair:
opaque fresh : Set string → string
axiom fresh_def (s : Set string) : FINITE s → fresh s ∉ s
findings.lean_check:
import CandleLean.HolSyntaxExtra

namespace Candle

example : fresh UNIV = (select (fun (f : Set string → string) => ∀ s : Set string, FINITE s → f s ∉ s)) UNIV := rfl

end Candle
findings.hol4_check: !w:string. ?f:(string set -> string). (!s. FINITE s ==> f s NOTIN s) /\ f UNIV = w
